title: Louis the humble man, and his last days in hospital
summary: Marge says Louis stayed down to earth, amazed at the limousine, and was closest to Zutty. In his last days Louis asked for Zutty at the hospital, where they sat with him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well I always say that, there's maybe one thing I can say, maybe Louis got commercial. But Louis was still a humble man. He was really an earth man to the very end. He told Zuddy when come and pick him up and take him he was going to take him to the Carson Show. And he said, yes man, he said, you know when I do them shows they send a big black limousine for me. Yes, he said, they always send that big black limousine.

And I said, well why shouldn't they? But to Louis that was terrible. It was a big deal for him. And when he picked us up at the hotel and when we got in the car the chauffeur jumped out, you know. It was a Carey limousine, and helped Zuddy in the car. Louis said to Zuddy, look at this, isn't this something, isn't this something?
Now I mean you know that showed that he was still.... Didn't realise how big he was you know. He really didn't. He was just such a down to earth, down to earth man.
Well I think he, yes I think he always seemd to me when.... I never really knew Louis that well. I mean he was always sweet with me.
We were very close. Like always saying he was like a brother and all. I think he was closer to Zutty than anybody. Yes, I really do. I think he was........

In his last days we were with him. And we knew, he sent for us to come to the hospital and they wouldn't let anybody in. And Lucille called and said Marge would you do me a favor? And I said anything, I told you Lucille, anything you want me to do. So, I want you to bring Zutty over to the hospital, tomorrow. I said, well we've been over there but they said no, couldn't have company. Said well bring him over tomorrow Louis is asking for him.

And we went over to the hospital. We were just among the few who got in that hospital. We sat with him. We talked with him. He wouldn't even let the nurses make him lie down. He wanted to sit on the side of the bed. And he sat there and he talked to us. Then he wanted to lie down and I went to get the nurse and I couldn't find her. And I said, Louis I'll put you, I'll fix you. I'll put your pillows back. And I lifted, he couldn't even lift his legs up.

I lifted one leg up and he'd say, now lift the other one. I said, you don't think I'm going to leave it down do you? (LAUGHTER). And I talked to him just like he was Zutty you know. And he laughed and all that. He wanted Zutty to the bitter end.
And we have such lovely memories of him. And we'd laugh and we'd laugh and we laughed. And someday you've just got to hear that tape that he made of he and Zutty talking.
